result.title: Online State-Representation Adaptation under Synthetic Interaction-Cue Remapping
result.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Code and synthetic data are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24329690
result.summary: When cues change what they predict, continuing to update a learned mapping may help an agent choose the appropriate action. We tested this in a one-step synthetic task by comparing a logistic state predictor that continued to learn from state labels with the same predictor frozen at transfer. We evaluated ten conditions in six held-out environments, with 1,296 paired runs per condition and 1,296,000 transfer records in total. Late action accuracy was 93.39% with online updates and 64.63% with frozen coefficients, a paired difference of 28.76 [8.73, 53.19] percentage points (95% environment-bootstrap interval). A direct policy reached 95.65% using the same predictions with a different action threshold. A contextual bandit reached 94.23% and earned more cumulative utility than the adaptive predictor. The bandit used the reward of its chosen action, which in this task reveals the true state when combined with that action. Weights based on development history lowered cumulative utility relative to neutral weights (difference -3.45 [-4.48, -2.43]). The adaptive predictor outperformed its frozen counterpart in late accuracy in each of the six test environments. The other comparisons show how the choice of action threshold and the information available in feedback affect what can be attributed to online adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在一步式合成任务中，比较持续用状态标签在线学习的状态预测器与在迁移时冻结系数的同一预测器，并对照直接策略与 contextual bandit，考察线索—结果映射改变后动作准确率与累积效用的变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 「在线更新 vs 冻结」「动作阈值」「反馈中是否含真状态信息」的对照设计，可能为 LVR 中把增益归因于 latent 状态更新、答案读出与反馈信息提供可核查的实验模板；但材料无视觉输入，迁移需自行论证。
